title: Noether normalization over a domain, up to inverting one nonzero element
statement: Let $R$ be an integral domain and $R\to S$ an injective ring map of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. For an $R$-algebra $T$ and $f\in R$ write $T_f$ for the ring of fractions $t/f^n$ ($t\in T$, $n\ge0$; $t/f^n=t'/f^m$ iff $f^u(tf^m-t'f^n)=0$ in $T$ for some $u\ge0$). Then there are an integer $d\ge0$, elements $y_1,\ldots,y_d\in S$ and an $R$-subalgebra $S'\subseteq S$ such that: (1) the $R$-algebra map $R[Y_1,\ldots,Y_d]\to S$, $Y_i\mapsto y_i$, from the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] is injective and its image $R[y_1,\ldots,y_d]$ is contained in $S'$; (2) $S'$ is a finitely generated $R[y_1,\ldots,y_d]$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; (3) there is a nonzero $f\in R$ such that the map $S'_f\to S_f$, $s/f^n\mapsto s/f^n$, induced by the inclusion is bijective.

proof.text: Apply the split-off generic-fibre construction, which supplies all data and surjectivity of the localization map.
The localization map induced by an inclusion of subalgebras is injective by IsLocalization.map_injective_of_injective and Subtype.val_injective. Pairing this with surjectivity gives bijectivity.

split_report.summary: Read Stacks 07NA (algebra.tex, lemma-Noether-normalization-over-a-domain) and its proof, and 00OY, 00GK, 02JJ which it cites. Statement kept (it is 07NA with 'S' finite over R[y]' as a finitely generated module and S'_f = S_f as bijectivity of the induced map). Proof in seven steps following 07NA: S_K = U^{-1}S (U = R minus 0) is a nonzero finite type K-algebra; Noether normalization over K (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-noether-normalization-field, exact match exists_finite_inj_algHom_of_fg) with the y_j moved into S by rescaling the variables (instead of the 'Moreover' of 00OY, which Mathlib lacks); injectivity of R[Y] -> S; monic equations over K[Y] by lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral; clearing denominators written out in K and in S; S' finite by lem-weil-pbc-finite-of-integral-generators (Mathlib leaf); S'_f -> S_f bijective written out directly. All three clauses are used by the citer lem-weil-pbc-derivation-nonzero-on-non-pth-power (Step 3). The existing node lem-zl-noether-normalization-field (unit sk-i-real-normalization, outside this unit's route, unsplit) states the same field case; the new leaf is in this unit and the duplication is reported.
